title: Which from-idea links the rebase leaves alone beyond URLs, anchors and fences
body:
**Chose:** root-absolute targets (`/x.md`) and images stay as written; links inside inline code spans are rebased like prose; anchors and `"title"` parts are kept. The rewriter is `migrate::rebase_links`, built on `edit_links`, whose callback now also receives the whole link source.
**Over:** also skipping inline code spans, or giving `with_idea` its own link parser.
**Because:** the slice names only URLs, `#` anchors and fences, and `check` resolves inline-code links too, so rebasing them keeps `docs check` green. Reusing `edit_links` keeps one link grammar.
**Undo:** add a code-span skip in `rebase_prose` (`src/docs/migrate.rs`).

title: Which spaces may a long commit subject be cut at?
body:
**Chose:** a space is a cut point only when at least two words of the text come before it. `fix(015): CI <60-char check>` cuts at 50 chars, and `feat(015): slice-07 Cards—tabs—…` cuts at 50 rather than at `slice-07`.
**Over:** any space after the `kind(NNN): ` prefix. Under that reading the space after `CI` fits, so the subject would be the bare `fix(015): CI`. That contradicts the slice's acceptance that a spaceless 60-char check name gives exactly 50 chars.
**Because:** the slice's acceptance and the PRD's literal wording disagree on the CI case. A subject that stops after its lead word (`CI`, `slice-NN`) says nothing.
**Undo:** drop the two-word filter in `cut` (`src/commit.rs`) and change the CI expectation in its unit test.

title: Where log add names the main tree's log path
body:
**Chose:** when `docs log add` writes outside the cwd's repo, it prints `{absolute log.jsonl path} updated` on stderr. Stdout still holds only the entry's id.
**Over:** adding the path to stdout, next to the id.
**Because:** callers capture the printed `AD-n`/`BLOCK-n` from stdout, so a second line there would break them. `set` has no such reader, so its stdout message carries the absolute path.
**Undo:** move the `outside_cwd` line in the `LogVerb::Add` arm of `src/cli/docs.rs` to stdout.

title: check in a lane when main has no folder for the feature
body:
**Chose:** `check` reads a feature's `state.toml` and `log.jsonl` from the main tree's same-named folder only when that folder exists. If it does not, it reads the lane's files (`board::board_dir`).
**Over:** always reading main's files, which reports E-STATE-INVALID for a feature that exists only in the lane.
**Because:** a feature that is new in the lane has its board files only in the lane.
**Undo:** drop the `is_dir` filter in `board::board_dir`.
